components: shim (mcpsnoop -- <server>): spawned in place of the real server, forwards stdio bytes verbatim while copying each JSON-RPC frame to the hub
hub + TUI (mcpsnoop, no args): rendezvous with the shim via a well-known socket and on-disk logs, renders live traffic
replay engine (key r) -- reruns a captured call against a fresh, isolated copy of the server
HTTP reverse-proxy mode for streamable-HTTP servers (--target/--listen)
demo subcommand (scripted session, nothing to set up)

commands.text: claude mcp add everything -- mcpsnoop -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything

architecture_facts: sits in the actual data path as a transparent proxy, unlike the official MCP Inspector which connects as its own separate client and never sees real client-server traffic
the shim forwards stdio bytes verbatim while mirroring each JSON-RPC frame to the hub over a well-known socket plus on-disk logs, so startup order does not matter
streamable-HTTP servers run through mcpsnoop as a reverse proxy instead of a stdio shim
single Go 1.26 binary, zero runtime dependencies, TUI built on Charm's Bubble Tea stack with vim-style keybindings
replay reruns a captured tool call against a fresh, isolated copy of the server, not the live one
surprising_detail: The README bakes a growth loop into its own install instructions: Homebrew core only accepts projects past a stars/forks/watchers notability bar, so the docs directly ask readers to star the repo so the tap-free `brew install mcpsnoop` can qualify -- the distribution channel is wired to the star count.
